title: Cooperation and the Operators union
summary: Reference remuneration arithmetic and a fictional simulator exist; genuine union participation, collective authority and signed Assignment integration remain unfinished.

goals.title: Reference remuneration tools
goals.description: Confirmed achieved scope covers the shared calculation library and its local fictional simulator. Membership and recovery, genuine completion admission, Operator-authorized ballots, collective decisions, approved amendments and integration with exact signed Assignments remain outside these completed checkpoints. The calculator's acceptance candidate is separate from the Assignment protocol's signed Contract; calculating a settlement minimum does not authorize or execute payment. The future Goals below propose how to develop the questions preserved in the Operators union notes; their steps, ownership and implementation order remain undefined.

milestones.title: Reference remuneration calculator and verification boundaries
milestones.description: Native Rust and the WASM host API share protocol-v1 remuneration arithmetic. The 26 September synthetic validation checkpoint is retained; the unified repository records further managed-Debian checks on 2 and 8 October. Required verification callbacks enforce the library boundary, but their approval cannot establish genuine membership, work, ballot consent, demand or collective agreement authority. Vote and acceptance constructors produce unsigned candidates; retained terms and approved-time settlement minima are reference behavior, without a live ledger, signed Assignment integration or payment execution.
acceptance: The shared native/WASM core implements exact minor-unit arithmetic, equal initial weight per performance, completion-time decay, separate upper weighted medians, scope isolation, participation thresholds, baseline fallback and a bounded optional demand premium.

Personal quotes respect both minima; unsigned acceptance candidates retain their terms; approved overruns raise the settlement minimum proportionally and faster completion retains the accepted amount.

Historical synthetic checks cover rounding, duplicate and tampered records, retained snapshots and refusal of missing or denied verification callbacks. Evaluation requires policy, complete-ballot-set, individual-ballot and applicable demand approvals; settlement requires acceptance and working-time approvals. Real authentication remains the integrator's responsibility.

evidence.label: Protocol arithmetic, unsigned candidates and verification contract
Managed-Debian cooperation and browser checks, 2 October
Recorded cooperation WASM and 88 cooperation-group checks, 8 October

milestones.title: Local fictional scenario simulator and setup editor
milestones.description: The standalone browser simulator uses the shared Rust/WASM core with configurable fictional Operators, tasks, rates, policies and synthetic demand. Its consistency verifier authenticates no real participant or work. Hypothetical completions automatically add hypothetical ballots; policy edits are scenario controls, not member votes or adopted amendments. State lives in page memory and exports are unsigned. Timeline scrubbing hides future completions and acceptances but does not reconstruct earlier policy, personal-rate or demand settings. Historical scenario, configuration and real-browser checks establish this demonstration scope only.
acceptance: Fictional scenarios exercise personal-rate snapshots, repeat performances, task isolation, decay and support fallback, demand effects, rejected low offers, retained acceptance terms, approved overruns and faster completion through the shared core.

The setup editor validates drafts before applying a new scenario, supports discard and configuration import/download, and preserves exact currency minor units without exchange-rate conversion; snapshot export records the fictional scenario and its assumptions.

The 26 September validation records scenario/configuration tests and real-WASM browser checks, including setup editing, export, alternate currencies, narrow layouts and missing/invalid input failures. The 2 October unified-source record reports managed-Debian simulator/browser checks. These results establish no membership, authenticated ballot, collective authorization or live payment.

goals.title: Membership and genuine participation
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: define an understandable journey for joining, leaving, recovering access, performing qualifying work, authorizing a ballot and contesting a record. Hero 6 defines union eligibility, membership decisions and challenges, including participation by newcomers, people on leave and infrequent performers. Identity defines principal/key/device control and recovery assurance; neither account login, a face match nor an Assignment's Operator role establishes membership or authorizes ballot casting. Recovery must address historical attribution and duplicate voting identities without assuming a selected identity-proof method. Assignments composes the participant journey, Server side services would retain the authorized records, and Governance reviews institutional authority and the union's relationship to Non Verba. No enrollment, appeal or recovery mechanism is selected, and the steps remain to be scoped.

goals.title: Authentic completion ballots and auditable calculations
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: connect genuine eligible work and approved covered time to an Operator's explicit authorization of the complete rate/price ballot, then supply complete authenticated snapshots to the calculator. Hero 6 defines admission, challenges and correction for disputed work, duplicate identities, fabricated completions, replay and artificial task splitting; immutable v1 post-admission correction remains unresolved. Decide who attests each fact and snapshot completeness at an agreed cutoff. Stored completion, accepted sensor evidence, admitted ballot and complete calculation snapshot are separate decisions; sensor integrity alone proves neither genuine work nor ballot consent. Server side services would retain authorized membership/eligibility decisions, completions, approved-time records, exact ballots, effective agreement/policy versions and calculation inputs/receipts under these rules. Membership evidence remains conditional on the unselected method. Identity supplies participant/key authority; Durable infrastructure supplies authenticated submission, retry and status semantics without inventing new consent on retry. No operational verifier, ledger design or correction process is chosen.

goals.title: Member decisions and approved policy amendments
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: define how members propose, discuss, inspect, authorize and record a shared-rule change, with the required counterparty assent and an effective agreement/policy version. Hero 6 develops participation, dissent and collective approval requirements; Governance reviews their institutional authority, protected-rights safeguards and legal/accountable relationship to Non Verba. Decide how prospective amendments preserve already accepted terms through the separate Assignment amendment boundary. Constitutional, administrative and remuneration decisions need an explicit account of their authority; completion-ballot weighting must not silently govern every decision. Server side services would retain exact authorized revisions and authority references rather than acquire policy-making authority from database control. No approval threshold, representative body or amendment procedure has been adopted.

goals.title: Task definitions and shared remuneration policy
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: make the covered work unit, task/version boundaries and remuneration rules understandable to participants. Define the treatment of preparation, evidence production, additional work and expenses, and develop reviewable choices for baselines, support thresholds, decay and the price/time aggregation rules. Examine how granularity, equipment, experience and concentrated participation affect the result. Decide whether to enable the optional demand premium and, if enabled, how demand and capacity are scoped, observed and authenticated; service-side observation records remain conditional on that choice. Simulator defaults select no real price or voting policy. Hero 6 defines the collective remuneration scope; Assignments owns task/quote presentation and the exact signing journey, while qualification, safety and coverage admission need their separate participant, incident/insurance and Governance decisions. Adopting remuneration choices requires the union's approved decision process. No task catalog or production policy values are selected.

goals.title: Collective remuneration in exact signed Assignments
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: trace a reviewed collective agreement, its effective policy version and calculated remuneration into the exact Assignment Contract reviewed and signed by the parties. Hero 6 owns collective policy, ballot admission and auditable remuneration inputs/calculations; Assignments composes exact Contract review/signing and completion consent. Define the mapping from unsigned calculator candidates without allowing later votes, rates or policies to replace accepted terms. Dispute procedure defines the permitted process, consent and consequences for contested time, extra work, scope changes, cancellation, partial completion and expenses. Preserve attributed original claims, approved/disputed inputs and their authority/version references so a corrected input is distinguishable from a new contractual effect. Server side services would retain the records and supply any separately authorized payment integration. Evidence acceptance, ballot consent, formula approval, Assignment acceptance and payment authority remain distinct. Priors declarations concern reasoning, not union voting influence. No integration format, correction mechanism or operational payment authority is agreed.

goals.title: Member privacy and accountable calculation audit
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: define who may inspect membership, personal rates, completions and ballots, and how participants can verify aggregate calculation receipts or challenge a result without unnecessary disclosure. Price/time pairs can reveal a personal rate even without an explicit rate field. Hero 6 defines union-specific disclosure, challenge and correction requirements with Identity's common sensitive-data rules; membership records must not silently require centralized identity or biometric evidence. Server side services would enforce selected access, retention and correction rules for participation records and calculation snapshots, while Governance addresses independent accountability. Case scrutiny or incident disclosure has its own recipient/purpose authority and does not automatically expose all member records or authorize underwriting reuse. Economic vote expiry remains separate from data deletion. No retention period, auditor role, membership-evidence store or access policy is adopted.

goals.title: Participation research and a bounded union pilot proposal
goals.description: Proposed future Goal: use explicitly fictional scenarios to examine frequent and occasional performers, newcomers, leave, limited or concentrated participation, disputed work and manipulated inputs, then identify what further evidence would assess fairness, comprehension, usability and operational trust. Scenario findings would inform discussion rather than adopt policy or prove a functioning union. Hero 6 develops the union-specific research and pilot proposal, including participants, covered work, counterparties and member needs for administration, representation and funding. Governance addresses institutional/financing constraints, organizational form, reviewed adoption and the overall offering's pilot/launch authority; the union proposal supplies no independent launch permission. Assignments owns participant comprehension of the connected journey, APK owns Android implementation/physical client acceptance, and service/workflow Heroes supply their operational capabilities. No pilot scope, study protocol, success criteria, dependency order or launch commitment is selected.
